lines.text: A seventy-three-year-old homeless man has recurrent sore throats that did not improve after a course of antibiotics. He comes to A and E with a lump on the left side of his neck. What is the likely diagnosis?
The answer is a pharyngeal pouch.
This seventy-three-year-old man keeps getting sore throats, again and again.
The grey cloud of sore throat keeps circling back.
(sigh) He finished his antibiotics, but they did not help at all.
Now he points to a lump on the left side of his neck.
Here is why. The inferior constrictor has two parts, thyropharyngeus above and cricopharyngeus below.
Between them is a weak gap, Killian's dehiscence. The mucosa pouches out through it.
Remember: an older patient with a neck lump and stubborn throat symptoms has a pharyngeal pouch.
A twenty-five-year-old man discovers a hard lump on his left testicle. His GP arranges a beta-hCG blood test, which is positive. What is the likely diagnosis?
This twenty-five-year-old man has just found something worrying.
It is a hard lump in his left testicle.
His beta-hCG blood test comes back positive.
(laugh) Meet the teratoma, a tumour made of many cell types, with tooth, hair, bone and muscle all mixed together.
These cells come from one or more of the three germ layers, from abnormal pluripotent cells.
Teratomas belong to the non-seminomatous germ cell tumours.
Remember: a hard testicular lump in a young man with a positive beta-hCG suggests teratoma.
